acceptance: Measured plan and result comparison for Redshift TPC-DS with and without declared keys, recorded in the registry notes.
Measured effect (or documented absence) of RELY on Snowflake and Databricks, recorded in the registry notes.
context: Source: tpcds-composite-primary-keys-20261001 audit remainder, PR #2631 (2026-10-04). Blocked on live approval from the owner.
description:
## Problem (unmeasured; documented as a limit in PR #2631)
The TPC-DS composite-key item recorded audit notes in `capability_registry.py` from vendor documentation and code reading only: Redshift's planner is documented to use informational keys and assume they are valid, so a wrong key can return wrong results; Snowflake and Databricks emit no `RELY` today. Whether the keys change plans or results for the TPC-DS queries on those platforms was not measured, because that needs live clusters.

## Change
With explicit owner approval for each live run (command, maximum runtime, log path, stop condition), compare TPC-DS plans and results with and without the keys on Redshift, and test the effect of `RELY` on Snowflake and Databricks. Update the capability-registry notes with measured facts.

## Guardrails (must preserve)
- No live cloud runs without explicit approval stating the command, maximum runtime, log path and stop condition.

## Process guardrails
- One PR per item against `develop`, via the AGENTS.md worktree flow.
- Verification ladder: `uv run -- python -m pytest -m fast -q`, `uv run -- ruff check .`, `uv run -- ruff format --check .` and `uv run -- ty check`; then `make pr-preflight` and `make pr-open`.
- Stage explicit paths; never `git add -A`. Re-read every anchor before editing.
